narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
intent: To demonstrate that income inequality, measured by the ratio of household income at the 90th percentile to the 10th percentile, has increased steadily since 1980.

units.meaning: The relative income-inequality measure is higher in 2019 than in 1980, showing an overall upward trend.
accepted_routes: The inequality indicator rises overall from 1980 to 2019.
The series ends higher than it starts.
There is a net upward movement from the first to the last benchmark year.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Both the 1980 and 2019 relative-value marks must be visible, and the 2019 mark must be higher than the 1980 mark.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video convey an overall upward trend from 1980 to 2019?

units.meaning: The rise is steady: each successive benchmark year has a higher relative_value than the previous year (1980 < 1990 < 2000 < 2010 < 2019).
accepted_routes: The indicator increases at every benchmark step.
No benchmark year is lower than the one before it.
The series is monotonically rising across the listed years.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Consecutive benchmark-year relative-value marks must appear in increasing order, with no downward step between them.
units.reviewer_question: Must the clip show monotonic/steady increase across all consecutive benchmark years, not just an overall endpoint rise?

units.meaning: The endpoint relative values are 0.4314 in 1980 and 0.5972 in 2019.
accepted_routes: The series starts at 0.4314 in 1980 and finishes at 0.5972 in 2019.
The 1980 value is 0.4314; the 2019 value is 0.5972.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The clip must display or state the two endpoint relative values, and their 1980/2019 timing must be clear.
units.temporal_anchor: since about 1980; has also been rising
units.reviewer_question: Must the exact endpoint relative values be stated/displayed, or is the trend shape enough?

units.meaning: The total change from 1980 to 2019 is +0.1658 relative-value units.
accepted_routes: The measure is 0.1658 higher in 2019 than in 1980.
The total rise is 0.1658 relative-value units.
From 0.4314 to 0.5972, the net increase is 0.1658.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The difference between the 2019 and 1980 relative-value marks must be shown or stated as an increase.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video quantify the total increase, or is showing the upward shape sufficient?

units.meaning: 2019 has the highest relative_value (0.5972) and 1980 has the lowest (0.4314) among the listed benchmark years.
accepted_routes: The highest point is 2019 at 0.5972; the lowest is 1980 at 0.4314.
The series peaks at the final benchmark year and starts at its minimum.
2019 is the maximum and 1980 is the minimum.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The 2019 relative-value mark must be visibly the highest and the 1980 mark visibly the lowest among the five benchmark years.
units.reviewer_question: Must the clip explicitly identify the maximum and minimum benchmark years?

optional_valid: The clip may name the metric as the 90th/10th household income ratio, provided it uses only relative comparisons and no absolute income values.
The clip may note that the five years are benchmark observations rather than annual data.
The clip may display intermediate benchmark values 1990=0.4788, 2000=0.5024, and 2010=0.5546.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal claims that policy, demographics, or specific events caused the rise.
Absolute household income, dollar amounts, percentages, or 90th/10th ratio values not in the table.
Extrapolating beyond 2019 or claiming the ratio will keep rising.
Claiming annual data or that every year from 1980 to 2019 rose; the table only has benchmark years.
Claiming the measure doubled; 0.5972 / 0.4314 is about 1.38 times the 1980 relative value.
notes: All numeric claims are taken from relative_value or computed as differences/comparisons of relative_value cells. Because the table is relative-only, avoid absolute ratio, dollar, percentage, or count statements.
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
